subject: Sep 30 per-request floor applied to embed calls — request for attribution export
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@pairwise.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@pairwise.ai
Date: 2025-10-09T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Unexpected per-request floor on Sep 30 invoice

Hi Grace,

We're reviewing our September charges and noticed a line item on the 9/30 invoice that looks like a per-request floor was applied to a batch of embedding calls (approximately 14k calls). The charge shows a higher effective per-call than our agreed unit price and is labeled in the portal as "fallback_rateband/min_charge_per_request."

I attached a screenshot of the billing UI and included our billing contact on cc. Can you help us understand:
- Why the fallback/min charge was applied (we believe our account should be on the negotiated per-embed price band)
- A full sample export for the 9/30 window (per-request granularity) so we can reconcile the counts

We'd like this resolved before we process payment. If this was an error, we will request a credit; if not, we need line-level evidence for our internal finance team.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform
Pairwise AI

Attachment: screenshot-metering-ui.png (png)

From: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@pairwise.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-09T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected per-request floor on Sep 30 invoice

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. I've looped in Ben (billing ops) and Kimberly (finance) to pull the raw export and confirm the rateband decision.

Quick asks from our side to speed this up:
- Can you confirm the HubSpot deal id or the contract amendment that contains the per-embed price? I have PW-3421 but want to be sure.
- Do you have any request IDs or sample timestamps from the window where you see the higher effective rate? That will let us do a direct match against our logs.

Ben/Kim — can you check for any legacy flag on Pairwise that would trigger a min_charge_per_request for bursts or if there was a cross-tenant fallback to a higher band on 2025-09-30 23:00-23:59 UTC? If we find a misrouting/config, default next step is a retroactive credit and a full evidence export.

Grace
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@pairwise.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-09T12:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected per-request floor on Sep 30 invoice

Elena — we pulled the telemetry and a short summary:

- Root cause: During a short concurrency spike at 2025-09-30T23:18:xxZ, Pairwise's requests hit a fallback policy tied to a legacy rateband labeled "fallback_rateband_v1." The runtime applied a per-request minimum charge for a ~4-minute window while autoscaler spin-up adopted a different instance class. This is documented behavior for that fallback policy but should not have applied if the account had the active override flag set.

- Evidence: attached is a 1k-line sample of the per-request export for 2025-09-30 (usage-export-2025-09-30-sample.csv). Columns include request_id, timestamp_utc, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, applied_rateband, applied_unit_cost_usd. In the sample you can see ~320 requests with applied_rateband == fallback_rateband_v1 and applied_unit_cost_usd shows the min-charge applied. Full export is large; we'll provide a shared Drive link if you want the whole day.

- Next steps proposed:
  1) We can provide the full day export to Pairwise for internal reconciliation.
  2) If Pairwise confirms these requests should have been billed at your contracted band (deal PW-3421), we will issue a retroactive credit for the delta between fallback_rateband_v1 charges and your contracted unit price, capped to the affected window.
  3) Operational fix: we will add an additional pre-check to prevent legacy fallback for accounts with an active override flag and run a one-off job to re-evaluate the 9/30 window for other potential misclassified requests.

I'll upload the full CSV to Drive and share a link here in an hour. For now I attached a sample subset.

Ben Carter
Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: usage-export-2025-09-30-sample.csv (csv)

From: Elena Morales <elena@pairwise.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace_occonnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@pairwise.ai, legal@pairwise.ai
Date: 2025-10-09T15:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected per-request floor on Sep 30 invoice

Thanks Ben — received the sample and the explanation. We're going to do a quick internal reconciliation against the sample; if the full export confirms misclassification we will accept a retro credit. To move this to resolution:

- Please provide the full export link (per-request CSV for 2025-09-30, ideally split by 1-hour chunks).
- Please confirm the maximum creditable window you will consider (your note said "capped to the affected window" — clarify whether that means the 4-minute spike only or up to 1 hour on either side).
- We'll need a short written confirmation that the operational fix you proposed will be put in place and a timeline (so our procurement/legal team can close the ticket). If credit is agreed, billing will require a short amendment to PW-3421 (one paragraph) and DocuSign routing to our finance contact.

Cc'ing our billing and legal to keep visibility.

Elena
Head of Platform, Pairwise AI
